proposed_widenings.name: triggered passive weapon rider family for magic items
proposed_widenings.justification: Sword of Sharpness is not an always-on passive grant and not an activated ability. Its mechanics are conditional weapon-hit and critical-hit riders attached to wielding the item. Current MagicItemMechanics only allows passive or activation, so any encoding would misstate timing or action economy.
proposed_widenings.evidence: When you attack an object with this magic weapon and hit, maximize your weapon damage dice against the target. When you attack a creature with this weapon and roll a 20 on the d20 for the attack roll, that target takes an extra 14 Slashing damage and gains 1 Exhaustion level.

proposed_widenings.name: trigger variant for natural-20 weapon attack
proposed_widenings.justification: The creature rider keys off a natural 20 on the d20, not merely a hit. Existing on-hit trigger shapes only express weapon_hit or melee-only weapon_hit, so they cannot distinguish this stricter trigger.
proposed_widenings.evidence: When you attack a creature with this weapon and roll a 20 on the d20 for the attack roll

proposed_widenings.name: maximize_weapon_damage_dice
proposed_widenings.justification: The object rider replaces the rolled weapon damage dice result with its maximum value. Existing atoms can add damage or modify d20 rolls, but they cannot maximize an already-resolving weapon damage roll.
proposed_widenings.evidence: maximize your weapon damage dice against the target

proposed_widenings.name: increment leveled exhaustion by 1
proposed_widenings.justification: apply_condition with condition=exhaustion only captures presence of the condition, not gaining one additional exhaustion level. Sword of Sharpness needs an incremental leveled-condition effect.

notes: No content file was authored. The item's primary mechanic is a passive triggered weapon rider, and MagicItemRecord currently has no honest family for that shape. Secondary gaps remain even if such a family existed: no natural-20 trigger variant, no representable maximize-weapon-damage-dice effect, and no leveled exhaustion increment effect.
